name: Emochi
tagline: AI character chat app where you talk to (and create) persona-driven bots for open-ended roleplay.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical core here is not hard: a system prompt holding a persona, a chat loop, a rolling summary for memory, and a table of characters you wrote yourself. An agent can put that in front of you in an afternoon, and for one person with three favorite characters it is genuinely enough. What it cannot hand you is the shared character library other people filled in, the tuning and prompt scaffolding that keeps a bot in voice across a long session, or a phone app you actually reach for on the couch. You also inherit a hard dependency on somebody's inference endpoint, which means either an API key with a bill attached or a local model that will feel noticeably duller. So: real personal version, yes, minus the part where content shows up without you writing it.
coreLoopDIY: A local chat app where you define characters with a persona and greeting, talk to them against an LLM endpoint, and keep history plus a rolling memory summary per conversation.
requirements: An API key for an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, or a local model runner like Ollama
Node 20+ and a willingness to write your own character personas
Somewhere to host it if you want it on your phone (or just use the browser)
whatYouLose: The library of characters other people made, which is most of why these apps are sticky
Persona tuning that holds voice over hundreds of messages instead of drifting into generic assistant
A real mobile app with push, voice, and offline-ish behavior
Content moderation decisions made by someone other than you, for better and worse
Images, avatars, and any generated media attached to characters
moatNotes: The character catalog is user-generated, so the moat is other users, not code. Your own build starts at an empty table.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody wants to write the characters. The paid product is a browsing experience: you open it bored, scroll a catalog someone else populated, and start talking in ten seconds. A self-built version inverts that, you now have to be the author before you can be the audience, and most people quit at that step. The subscription also covers inference you would otherwise pay for directly, plus a phone app, which is where this category is actually used.
notes: Building the engine is easy, building the appetite is not. Write two characters you actually like before deciding whether you needed the subscription.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI character chat app called "personachat" in this empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, created on first run
- Chat completions against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, configured by env: OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, MODEL_NAME (default to a small chat model). Put them in .env.local and read them server-side only. Never ship a key to the client.

Data model:
- characters: id, name, avatar_emoji, persona (long text), greeting, example_dialogue (optional text), temperature, created_at
- conversations: id, character_id, title, created_at
- messages: id, conversation_id, role (user|assistant|system), content, created_at
- memories: id, conversation_id, summary text, updated_at

Features that are in scope:
- Character list page with create, edit, duplicate, delete. A form with name, emoji, persona, greeting, example dialogue, temperature slider.
- Chat page per conversation: streaming assistant replies via the Edge-free Node route, message bubbles, autoscroll, retry last reply, edit or delete any message, and a "start over" button.
- Prompt assembly on the server: system prompt built from persona + example dialogue + the current rolling memory summary, then the last N messages that fit a token budget (approximate by characters, do not add a tokenizer dependency).
- Rolling memory: after every 10 messages, call the model once to update memories.summary for that conversation. Show the summary in a collapsible panel and let the user edit it by hand.
- Export a conversation to markdown, and export/import all characters as JSON.
- Seed the DB with two example characters so the app is not empty on first run.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Accounts, auth, multi-user, analytics, telemetry, payments
- Image generation, voice, a native mobile app, any public character browsing or sharing

Deliver: working npm run dev, a README with setup and a .env.local.example, and honest error states when the model endpoint is unreachable or the key is missing.
